title: Opal: Compact capacity dashboard + runtime controls
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact, scannable dashboard surface and inline controls for Dedicated capacity customers. Opal focuses on three core surfaces: a) health and utilization strip for GPU allocations, b) quick autoscale and burst controls with safe defaults and rollback affordances, and c) per-route cost/lantency hotspots tied to tenant routes. The goal is to enable on-call and platform engineers to triage capacity anomalies, apply safe adjustments within SLA guardrails, and immediately see cost delta estimates for changes.
design_goals: Surface actionable health signals in <3s glance time
Enable safe single-click scaling actions with preview and undo
Make cost impact visible before applying changes
Fit into the existing Console layout with minimal vertical real estate
constraints: Must reuse console token-level metric primitives and color tokens
Work within current permission model (only pool-owners and ops roles get action buttons)
Actions must trigger audit events and appear in the rollout history panel
acceptance_criteria: Compact 'Opal' strip shows per-allocation GPU utilization, queue length, and SLO status
Action controls (Scale Up/Down, Enable Burst, Revert) are available to users with correct RBAC and create an audit log entry
Cost preview shows estimated $/hour delta and percent latency change before apply
Design includes mobile-friendly responsive behavior for screen widths down to 768px
Figma prototype demonstrates the complete happy path and two failure modes (insufficient capacity and rollback)
decisions: Use compact ribbon layout (left: identification, middle: metrics strip, right: actions)
Autoscale quick actions use a 3-step confirmation modal for P0 pools and inline for non-P0
Burst enablement will show a soft quota preview and auto-schedule a fallback to pre-burst capacity after configured window
tradeoffs: Compact view limits visible historical context; we provide drill-through to a full timeline to compensate
Inline actions reduce clicks but increase risk; we mitigate with RBAC and confirmation flows
Showing cost estimates requires calling an experimental estimator API; fallback shown when estimator unavailable

user_flows: Triage flow: open Console > Opal strip highlights SLO breach > click 'Investigate' > drill to timeline > apply scale-up with cost preview
Emergency flow: on-call receives alert > opens Opal strip > 'Enable Burst' inline control with 3-step confirmation > system schedules fallback and logs audit entry
usability_notes: Text density reduced: replace labels with icons + tooltip for frequent users
Color mapping: green/yellow/red for SLO, purple accent for burst-enabled state
Keyboard shortcuts: support focus+enter to apply common actions for power users
